context:
Goal: a builder cannot drop work an earlier commit of its own lane added, unless the commit says why.
Problem (rule): your ruling names a new excuse line, but the check already has one; two names for one excuse break your one-home rule.
Based on (read): the silent-undo check and the guard both accept only Drops-lines: today.
Based on (measured): today's check passes two commits from this morning that dropped a lane's own earlier work, so the gap is real.
Departs from: main, where Drops-lines: excuses only dropping main's work — it also excuses dropping the lane's own earlier work.
holds: Which excuse line the lane builds; it builds option a meanwhile.

lastAnswer.note: Removes: was the advisor's word, not mine. One excuse line. (owner, chat, via the coordinator)

options.gain: One excuse line, no guard change; builders learn one form.
options.how: The check also reads Drops-lines: when a builder drops its own lane's earlier work.
options.label: Reuse Drops-lines
options.lose: It names a file, not one test case, and it is not the word Removes: you used.

options.gain: Your word, and it can name one test case.
options.how: A new Removes: line excuses only the drop of the lane's own earlier work.
options.label: Add Removes
options.lose: Two excuse lines for one check, a change to what the guard accepts, and more review. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

ref: lane no-undo-lane-commits; decision silent-undo-check-design; inbox fb-1041-1
reply: Closed 10:54 CST: a, reuse Drops-lines. Home: decision silent-undo-check-design, written by lane no-undo-lane-commits.
short: excuse line for dropping lane work
title: When a builder drops work its own lane added, which line excuses it: the existing Drops-lines line, or a new Removes line?
why: Your 10:41 CST ruling says builders never undo earlier lane work unless the commit says so, and names a new Removes: line for that. The check that catches silent undos already accepts one excuse line, Drops-lines: <file> -- <reason>. Two names for one excuse would break your rule that each thing has one home.
